newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southeast power prices hold steady for Friday.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southeast power prices hold steady for Friday.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the U.S. Southeast held mostly steady Thursday with cooler weather expected to hold off until the lower power demand of the weekend, industry sources said.
Temperatures in the Southeast were forecast to be mild through Friday and then cool this weekend to four to 10 degrees Fahrenheit below normal.
More seasonable temperatures were expected to return to the region early next week.
Firm, peak power prices into Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) for Friday were steady in the $16.00-17.50 per megawatt hour (MWh) range, the sources said.
TVA's 1,065 MW Browns Ferry 2 nuclear power unit in Alabama was operating at near 60 percent of capacity as of early Thursday, and was expected to raise power to full capacity following some tests.
Browns Ferry unit 3, with an identical generating capacity, was at 81 percent power and coasting down to a refueling outage February 21.
Firm, off-peak power prices into TVA were said to be lower at $12.50-13.50 from $13.50-14.00 per MWh on Wednesday.
March TVA prices were talked steady in the $19.50-20.00 per MWh range, the sources said.
At the Georgia/Florida border, firm, peak power prices in 16 hour blocks for Thursday were talked lower at $18.50-19.50 from $19.50-20.50 per MWh on Wednesday.
Firm, off-peak power for Friday at the Ga./Fla. border was assessed unchanged at $14.00 per MWh.
